subject: Investigating recent p95/p99 warmup regressions on Hosted API autoscale
messages:
From: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@linearpay.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Severe p99 latency spikes during autoscale events (LinearPay prod)

Hi Grace,

We started seeing significant p95/p99 latency spikes this morning that correlate with your Hosted API autoscale events. During bursts at ~09:00–09:15 PST our p99 jumped from ~1.1s to 9–12s and error rate climbed from 0.1% to ~1.8%. Throughput dropped as requests queued. We believe this is tied to instances being added to the pool (cold-start behavior) — it has happened twice today at two separate scaleups.

Impact: customer-facing timeouts and slow checkout flows. We have request ids and small samples attached. Please treat this as P1 for LinearPay. We need:
- Immediate mitigation plan (fast workaround)
- ETA for a root-cause & permanent fix
- Any short-term configuration we can request via support

Attached: request-ids-sample-0308.txt (10 request ids), snippets of our timing graphs.

Thanks,
Sophie Chen
ProdOps, LinearPay

Subject: Re: Severe p99 latency spikes during autoscale events (LinearPay prod)

Hi all — quick triage notes (initial findings attached: warmup-trace-20270308.json):
- We see a clear correlation between pool scale-up events and sustained p99 regressions.
- Root correlate: new GPU workers are accepting traffic before model KV cache and CUDA kernels are fully warmed. Model weight mmap and JIT kernels account for ~3–6s of the spike in many cases; an extra 4–6s comes from KV cache cold misses and repeated micro-batching while the batcher adapts.
- In one case (req ids attached) the worker timed out on an RPC to a model shard and retried on a fallback worker adding ~2s.
- Observed differences by model variant: the quantized variant warms faster but yields small quality delta — customers on high-SLA plans are not automatically routed to quantized variants.

Short-term mitigations we can push within 1–3 hours:
1) Increase pre-warm concurrency for LinearPay's affined pool from 1 -> 3 (will keep 3 warm workers idle ready to accept traffic). Pros: immediate reduction in cold-starts. Cons: modest cost bump.
2) Enforce temporary routing to the quantized model variant during autoscale spin-up windows for their traffic. Pros: faster warmup; Cons: slight model quality delta.
3) Add a temporary client-side retry policy suggestion for LinearPay (slight backoff) and bump their timeout to tolerate 3s more during spinups.

I attached warmup traces and a small sample of request ids for more detailed debugging. Next steps: Jordan to push a short-term change (1) as a config toggle, Aditya to confirm with LinearPay on the cost implications.

Dylan
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Agree with Dylan. Quick action plan I'm putting into motion now:
- Toggle: pre-warm-concurrency=3 for LinearPay's pool (sched rollout in 10 minutes). This will keep 3 GPUs initialized and reduce cold-start surface.
- Canary: enable routing to quantized variant for 10% of traffic during warmup window to validate quality impact.
- Monitoring: add a short-lived alert on 'worker_warm_completed' latency and 'kv_cache_miss' rates to notify on any regressions.
- Timeline: rollout starts 10m, full effect ~15–25m.

I'll monitor and post traces to the Grafana panel. If the canary passes, we'll scale the quantized fallback to 100% for the warmup interval only.

Jordan

Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident update: warmup gap mitigations and next steps (LinearPay)

Summary for LinearPay & internal execs:
- What happened: p95/p99 regressions tracked to GPUs being added to pools while workers were not fully warmed (CUDA kernel JIT + weight mmap + KV cache cold misses). This produced ~6–12s p99 spikes in our hosted pool during autoscale.
- Immediate actions taken (Mar 8, 09:30–10:00 PST): pre-warm-concurrency increased 1->3 for LinearPay-affined pool; 10% canary routing to quantized variant during warmup windows; short client-side retry guidance issued. These actions reduced observed p99 to ~1.4s in rolling windows.
- Next steps (prod fixes):
  * Engineering: implement a faster worker warm-complete signal (optimize kernel JIT path and parallelize weight mmap) — owner: Dylan, ETA: 3 weeks for delivery and testing.
  * Product: consider a new tiering knob that lets customers opt-in to warm-concurrency SLAs — owner: Grace, ETA: roadmap Q2 planning.
  * SRE: incorporate warmup-aware routing & automatic temporary fallback to quantized variants during scale-ups — owner: Jordan, ETA: 2 weeks for safe rollout.
- Customer support/commercial: Aditya/Evelyn to confirm credit mechanics and communicate to LinearPay.

We're leaving the pre-warm-concurrency at 3 for their pool for now; if LinearPay prefers, we can revert and adopt a different mitigation.

Sophie/Daniel — apologies for the disruption. We'll share a detailed postmortem with traces and timelines within 5 business days.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
